title: Watchful, not anxious
hook: live each day ready and unafraid

segments.voice: Yesterday, not as those without hope: Paul assumes grief, and asks what it leans on. Your line was grieve, with hope. Whose sadness did you sit with? Day one thousand three hundred thirty.

It's late. The house is quiet, but nobody's gone to bed. The lamps are still lit, belts still fastened, shoes still on. The master of the house is at a wedding feast, and nobody knows when he'll be back. Midnight. Later. Toward morning. The servants aren't pacing or panicking. They're just awake, with the door within reach, so that the moment he knocks, it opens. Jesus tells this little scene in Luke's Gospel, and then he adds a twist so strange that it's easy to read right past it. The servants in that lit house are today's word.

First, the instruction. In the King James words: "Let your loins be girded about, and your lights burning." Dressed for action, lamp lit. In Mark, Jesus puts it in one word, and widens it: "And what I say unto you I say unto all, Watch." The Greek word behind watch means stay awake. Second, the twist. When the master gets home and finds them awake, what does he do? "He shall gird himself, and make them to sit down to meat, and will come forth and serve them." The master serves the servants. The one they've been waiting for turns out to be the one who waits on them. That changes what watching is. It isn't guarding against a punishment. It's staying up for someone who is coming home to feed you. Third, not anxious. The same Jesus says, "Take therefore no thought for the morrow: for the morrow shall take thought for the things of itself." And Paul writes, "Be careful for nothing." In the King James, careful means full of care, anxious, not cautious. So watchful and anxious are not the same thing. Anxiety stares at tomorrow. Watchfulness pays attention to now. Fourth, what watching looks like up close. In Gethsemane, Jesus takes three disciples a little way with him, asks them to watch with him, and goes on to pray. He comes back and finds them asleep: "What, could ye not watch with me one hour?" Then: "the spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak." Watching, there, isn't scanning the horizon. It's staying with someone, awake, in the hour that's here. Readiness, in these stories, is attention to now, and the good in front of you, done well.

Here's the practice: find today's good, and plan to do it well. Settle, and breathe. Notice if your mind is running ahead to tomorrow, or next month, or the end of everything. Let it come back to this day. Then ask: what's the ordinary good in front of me today? A meal to cook, a report to finish, a kid to pick up, a call to return. Choose one. If you pray, you can offer it to God as the thing you'd like to be found doing. If you don't, simply decide to do it with care. The bell holds the time.
Watchful. Awake and ready, lamp lit, for someone coming home. In the Gospels, it means doing today's good, without anxiety about tomorrow.

Your line: ready, not afraid. This week went from rest in peace, through a seed in the ground, a taunt to death, a city coming down, a face to face, and grief with hope, to a lamp left burning. Today, do the good you chose, and do it well. Day one thousand three hundred thirty.

howItsDone: Churches that keep Advent watch toward Christ's coming in that season, and in vigils and night prayers; Gospel stories of watchful servants are among its readings.

pairs: the master home from the wedding

careful there means full of care, anxious. Paul is saying: don't be anxious.

fork.setup: you're the master, home late from a wedding. you knock, and your servants open at once, lamps lit. what do you do?
options: inspect the house for anything left undone.
put on an apron, sit them down and serve them.
send them to bed and eat alone.
fork.reveal: "he shall gird himself, and make them to sit down to meat, and will come forth and serve them." the one they waited for waits on them.

original.note: Greek: watch, stay awake, Jesus's word in Mark 13:37.

trapdoor: what you thought: watchful means nervously scanning for the end of the world.
what it means: awake and ready, doing today's good well, without anxiety about tomorrow.
what a scholar hears: grēgoreite, stay awake, and Luke 12:37, where the master turns servant and waits on those who waited for him.
